Once upon a time, in a land far, far away, there lived a little girl named Lily. She was a curious and adventurous soul, always eager to explore the world around her. One day, she decided that she wanted to learn how to bake a cake. So, she went to the kitchen and began to gather all the ingredients she needed: flour, sugar, eggs, butter, and milk.

As she mixed the ingredients together, she realized that she needed to follow a recipe. She looked at the recipe book and saw that it had instructions for making a chocolate cake. But, as she read through the recipe, she noticed that it said "preheat the oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit." She didn't know what that meant, so she asked her mother for help.

Her mother explained that preheating the oven means heating it up before you put anything inside. She showed Lily how to turn on the oven and set the temperature to 350 degrees Fahrenheit. Then, she helped Lily mix the batter and put it into a baking pan.

While the cake was baking, Lily decided to make some frosting. She mixed powdered sugar, butter, and milk together until it was smooth and creamy. As she spread the frosting on top of the cake, she realized that she needed to wait for it to cool down before she could eat it.

But, as she waited, she started to wonder if she should add any extra ingredients to the cake. She thought about adding nuts or chocolate chips, but then she remembered that the recipe book said not to do that. She decided to leave the cake as it was, and when it was finally done, she took a big bite.

The taste was delicious! It was sweet and rich, with a nice texture. Lily couldn't believe how good it tasted. She knew that she had learned something new today, and she was excited to try baking again soon.

interpretation.verdict: INCONCLUSIVE — the control did not enter the regime it was meant to control for.
interpretation.why: The failing row's mechanism needs a baseline that is actually repetitive: the autoport's baseline scores unique_ratio 0.1449 (30 unique words in 207), i.e. it obeyed 'write a very repetitive story'. SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct ignored the instruction and wrote an ordinary story at unique_ratio 0.5298, so its type-token ratio was nowhere near the floor where a length increase can drag it below the 0.90 gate. Its PASS therefore says nothing about whether the gate is length-confounded.
interpretation.what_settles_it_instead: presence_penalty_row.json -> length_confound_test: truncating the autoport's own penalized response to the baseline's word count makes the two ratios exactly equal (1.0000), so the whole 0.8888 shortfall is the extra 88 words and none of it is reduced diversity.
interpretation.kept_because: it was run and it is a negative result; deleting it would leave the length-confound argument looking better supported than it is.
